verdict: The observed Article reset and subsequent zero-match Copy are explained by the product's active-page identity lifecycle: opening the video in a new active tab temporarily makes the stored capture non-current, unmounting the result Tabs; closing the opened tab returns to the capture page, which makes the retained capture current and mounts Tabs at its default Article pane. The driver clicked the intended video URL and intentionally closed the opened page before continuing. The receipt does not directly timestamp browser active-tab identity changes or opened.close(), so that native event-to-transition attribution remains inferred from the exact source path and reproduced component boundary.
